procedures.title: Refrigeration Incident Procedure (DEMO)
procedures.sourceLabel: Demo Kitchen A site procedure binder (DEMO, fictional)
procedures.body:
1. Record the reading, the time, the unit name and who saw it. Do not overwrite earlier readings.
2. Tell the manager on duty straight away.
3. Keep the door closed and move food only if the manager says so; label affected items 'HOLD - do not use'.
4. If it is not known how long food was above the site limit, do not use it or declare it safe. The manager decides what happens to it under the site's approved assessment.
5. Contact the site's approved refrigeration service provider (or find one if the site has none) and log the call.
6. Recheck the temperature and log it as a new reading. The manager closes the incident.

procedures.title: Allergen Incident Procedure (DEMO)
procedures.sourceLabel: Demo Kitchen A site procedure binder (DEMO, fictional)
procedures.body:
1. Stop: withhold the dish and any food made with the affected ingredient until it is verified.
2. Tell the manager on duty.
3. Contact the supplier for the full ingredient and allergen information and log who you spoke to and when.
4. Never tell a customer a dish is safe or allergen-free while the ingredient list is unavailable.
5. If anyone has symptoms of an allergic reaction, call emergency services (999) immediately.
6. Keep the packaging and batch details. The manager decides when the dish can return.

procedures.title: Cooking Temperature Check Procedure (DEMO)
procedures.sourceLabel: Demo Kitchen A site procedure binder (DEMO, fictional)
procedures.body:
1. Keep the failed reading in the log exactly as measured. Never edit or delete it.
2. Return the food to cooking and do not serve it.
3. Clean the probe and take a separate recheck reading, then log it as a new entry with the time.
4. If you are unsure about the probe or the result, use a second probe and tell the manager.
5. The responsible person decides whether the food can be served or must be thrown away and signs the entry.

procedures.title: Daily Food Safety Records Procedure (DEMO)
procedures.sourceLabel: Demo Kitchen A site procedure binder (DEMO, fictional)
procedures.body:
1. Write records at the time of the check only.
2. If a required record is missing, mark the slot 'MISSING RECORD' with the date. Do not fill it in afterwards from memory.
3. Never backfill or backdate a record.
4. Tell the manager on duty, who adds a dated note explaining the gap.
5. Agree on a fix (for example, a reminder at each check time) and log it as an action.

scenarios.title: Walk-in fridge reading 9°C
scenarios.description: At the evening check the walk-in fridge display reads 9°C. Nobody knows when it last read within the site limit.
reportedFacts: Fridge is full of prepped food for tomorrow
missingInformation: When was the last reading within the site limit?
Has the door been left open or is the unit faulty?
Which food items are stored inside?
scenarios.expectedOutcome: Isolate and hold the food, escalate to the manager, follow the site fridge procedure, then contact ColdLine (alpha) or use the external search (beta).
guardrails: Never declare the food safe when the exposure time is unknown
Do not set a global threshold from this one example
Contacting a provider needs a human click

scenarios.title: Unverified nut allergen in supplier sauce
scenarios.description: A new batch of satay-style sauce from the supplier arrived without its label. A customer with a nut allergy has asked about a dish that uses it.
reportedFacts: Customer has declared a nut allergy
missingInformation: Full ingredient and allergen list from the supplier
Has the sauce already been served today?
scenarios.expectedOutcome: Withhold the dish, tell the customer it cannot be confirmed, contact the supplier for the ingredient list and log it.
guardrails: Never tell a customer the dish is safe
Withhold until verified by the supplier
If anyone has symptoms, call emergency services (999) immediately

scenarios.title: Chicken temperature below configured site limit
scenarios.description: A probe reading on a tray of roast chicken is below the site-configured core minimum.
missingInformation: Was the probe cleaned and working?
Where in the thickest part was it measured?
scenarios.expectedOutcome: Keep the failed reading, return to cooking, take a separate recheck as a new entry, responsible person decides.
guardrails: Never overwrite or delete the failed reading
The recheck is a separate event
Only the responsible person decides whether to serve

scenarios.title: Missing daily food safety records
scenarios.description: At close, the cooking temperature log has only two of the four required entries for today.
missingInformation: Why were slots 3 and 4 not recorded?
Who was on the pass at those times?
scenarios.expectedOutcome: Show two real rows and two MISSING RECORD slots; the manager adds a dated note and a corrective action.
guardrails: Never backfill or backdate a record
Never invent item names for missing slots
The gap stays visible in the timeline

communityMessages.body: Not official advice, just experience: check the door seal and whether the evaporator fan is running or iced up. Don't keep opening the door. Your manager and your engineer make the call on the food.
When this happened to us we labelled everything HOLD and moved it to a working fridge only after our manager agreed. Log every reading as you go, it helps the engineer.

knowledgeCards.summary: Walk-in fridge reading rose above the site limit overnight (time unknown). Team held all food, escalated to the manager and called the approved contractor. Cause: iced evaporator. Learning: add a closing-time temperature check and a door-seal check to the weekly list.
